How to stop overthinking
at night
Write it all down before bed. Every worry, every task, every idea, on paper. Your brain lets go much more easily once it knows nothing will be forgotten.
Set a worry time earlier in the day. Fifteen minutes at 6pm to think through problems. When thoughts come at night, remind yourself you'll handle them then.
Get out of bed if you can't sleep. Read in another room with dim light for twenty minutes. Lying there fighting your thoughts only makes them louder.
Breathe slowly with a longer exhale. In for four seconds, out for seven. It tells your body it's safe, and a calmer body brings a calmer mind.
Give your mind something gentle to hold. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science before bed, and calm curiosity crowds out the anxious loops.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app before bed. History, art, science. Calm curiosity crowds out the anxious loops.

slides.texte_overlay: Move your body during the day. A tired body sleeps more easily. A walk, a workout or a swim makes your evenings calmer and your nights deeper and more restful.
Talk to someone if it doesn't stop. A friend, your doctor, a therapist. Thoughts that keep you up for weeks deserve real support, not silence.
